# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Reference POC-F7C299C469-49918

**Governing Policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026)
Policy link: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W530749089
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-07-31
**Reference number:** POC-F7C299C469-49918
**Procedure:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030

---

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for CPT 63030, a lumbar decompression procedure that my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented as medically necessary. I am asking that Cigna reconsider this decision because my medical records meet the criteria set out in Cigna's own policy, CMM-606, for initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy.

### Why I believe my records meet the plan's own criteria

Cigna's policy states that:

> "Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

My records document the following, which correspond to the categories the policy lists under this standard:

**Symptom pattern.** The policy lists as a relevant condition:

> "▪ symptoms worsen with standing and/or walking ▪ symptoms are alleviated with sitting and/or forward flexion"

My medical records show I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes before symptoms worsen, and I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf.

**Objective examination findings.** The policy lists, as findings supporting medical necessity:

> "◦ positive straight leg raise ◦ positive crossed straight leg raise ◦ positive femoral stretch test ◦ dermatomal sensory deficit ◦ functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness) ◦ reflex changes ◦ unremitting radicular pain into the lower extremity(ies) without concordant objective exam findings"

My exam notes document positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging. My MRI, dated 2026-06-08, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root — imaging findings that correlate directly with my clinical exam.
